TECHNOLOGY WORKING GROUP

You’re invited to help shape the Smart Property Data Trust Framework

Hello {{display_name}},

OPDA is bringing the property sector together to make UK property transaction
data interoperable, verifiable and consent-driven. Today, the same information
is repeatedly re-entered, translated and interpreted as it moves between
organisations and systems. The Smart Property Data Trust Framework will
establish a shared language and the technical foundations needed to exchange
and reuse that information with greater confidence.

Rather than forcing the whole property lifecycle into one universal model,
OPDA is creating a governed family of connected domain models. Domain working
groups shape meaning inside Finance and Banking, Conveyancing, Estate Agency,
Surveying and Valuation, Property Data Services and Property Technology. The
Interoperability Working Group aligns their boundaries and mappings.

The Technology Working Group works across all of those contexts. It brings
practical implementation experience to architecture, identifiers, provenance,
generated artefacts, conformance, compatibility and release readiness. It also
supports the trust-framework implementation work around APIs, sandbox services,
credentials, PKI, onboarding and developer guidance. Its job is to help prove
that the standard can work; it does not decide a domain’s business meaning or
ratify an OPDA Standard.

I ACCEPT
{{access_url}}

IMPORTANT: Sign in using the email account that received this invitation.
This invitation link is unique to that account, so please do not forward this
email.

YOUR CONTRIBUTION

There are three ways to take part:

1. Share implementation evidence. Contribute approved schemas, API definitions,
   architecture, integration guidance, test cases, compatibility findings and
   other technical material.
2. Review and test candidates. Challenge whether generated models, validation,
   schemas, APIs, forms and documentation are coherent, implementable and
   complete.
3. Join the discussion. Bring cross-sector implementation experience to the
   relevant Teams channel and keep replies in their existing threads.

HOW THE GROUP FITS

- Domain Working Groups decide business meaning inside each bounded context.
- The Interoperability Working Group owns the common boundary, context map,
  cross-domain mappings and shared conventions.
- The Technology Working Group provides cross-cutting technical review,
  implementation evidence and assurance.
- Compliance and Risk reviews privacy, security, law, competition,
  intellectual property and accessibility.
- The Executive Committee / Board holds the authority to ratify or withdraw an
  OPDA Standard.

OPDA’s end-to-end standards lifecycle is a proposed operating model, not yet an
operative rule. The group supports today’s technical implementation work and
helps shape the independent technical-review gate envisaged for future
releases.

HOW TO CONTRIBUTE SOURCE MATERIAL

1. Open your organisation’s source-intake folder. Sign in with the same company
   account that received SharePoint access, then open Source Material Intake and
   select your company folder:

   https://openpropertydataassociation.sharepoint.com/sites/TechnologySourceIntake/Incoming%20Source%20Material/Forms/AllItems.aspx?id=%2Fsites%2FTechnologySourceIntake%2FIncoming%20Source%20Material%2FBy%20Organisation

2. Organise your organisation’s material. You may create folders, upload files
   and create supporting documents inside your company folder.

3. Include a README. Add an index, provenance, relevant context, version and
   enough explanation for reviewers to understand the material and any
   restrictions on its use.

Your organisation’s folder is private to its approved contributors and OPDA
administrators. Other participating organisations cannot see it. Upload only
material your organisation is authorised to share with OPDA for this work.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE

Reply in threads. Threads keep each technical question, implementation finding
or review issue together and make the discussion manageable.

Open the most relevant channel and check whether a thread already covers the
subject. If it does, select Reply beneath the original post. Use Start a post
only for a genuinely new subject, with one clear issue per thread.

ACCESS AND PRIVACY

- Invitation only. Access is limited to people invited by OPDA. To invite
  additional colleagues, email smartdata@openpropdata.org.uk with their names,
  email addresses and organisations.
- Company accounts for SharePoint only. Source-intake access requires an
  approved company-domain account. This restriction does not prevent an
  invited participant from joining Teams with another account.
- Private organisation folders. Other organisations cannot see your
  submissions. Teams discussions and the ordinary Team files area are shared
  with the working group, so do not place restricted source material there.
- Not automatically public. Working material may inform review candidates, but
  OPDA will not treat a submission as permission to publish the source itself.

USEFUL SOURCE MATERIAL

- Schemas and interfaces: JSON Schema, OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, XML Schema
  and message or event definitions.
- Linked-data and validation artefacts: RDF, OWL, SKOS, SHACL, JSON-LD contexts
  and mapping examples.
- Architecture and trust: identity, credentials, PKI, authorisation, consent,
  provenance, audit and trust-framework patterns.
- Implementation evidence: integration findings, producer and consumer
  examples, compatibility reports, migrations, test cases and conformance
  results.
- Data structures: database schemas, entity-relationship diagrams, data
  dictionaries, field lists and non-production examples.
- Developer experience: sandbox and mock-service designs, onboarding guidance,
  technical documentation, diagrams and FAQs.

Audio and video files are not accepted. Recordings must be transcribed before
submission. Include the transcript’s date, speakers and context where known.

Upload the material itself—do not submit links. OPDA will not rely on links to
websites, cloud drives, shared folders or online documents. If authorised,
download or export the material and place the file in your company folder.

DO NOT SUBMIT

- Personal, customer or live property-transaction data.
- Passwords, API keys, credentials, private keys or other secrets.
- Material restricted by confidentiality, contract, licence or NDA.
- Executable software, active scripts or macros.
- Password-protected files, encrypted archives or compressed archives.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT

OPDA screens submitted material and uses approved evidence to develop
reviewable candidates. Domain working groups remain responsible for business
meaning. The Technology Working Group reviews technical integrity, feasibility,
generated outputs, compatibility and conformance, and feeds its findings into
the next iteration. A candidate does not become an OPDA Standard without the
required human review and authorised ratification.

Questions and technical feedback: use the most relevant channel and reply in
an existing thread whenever one covers the subject.

Additional invitations or private access problems:
smartdata@openpropdata.org.uk

Open Property Data Association · Technology Working Group
